name: PCI-SIG FAQ 'What bit rates does the PCIe 5.0 specification support and how does it compare to prior PCIe generations?'
notes: THE AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE ON DIRECTIONAL CONVENTION FOR THIS ENTIRE FAMILY. States the rate ladder per generation as 'Gigabits/second/Lane/DIRECTION of raw bandwidth' (2.5 / 5.0 / 8.0 / 16.0 / 32.0 for PCIe 1.0-5.0), and gives a worked example: 'A PCIe 5.0 Link consisting of 32 Lanes and operating at a bit rate of 32.0 GT/s provides an effective raw bandwidth of 128.0 Gigabytes/second IN EACH DIRECTION SIMULTANEOUSLY' - and 32 x 32 / 8 = 128.0, which proves the figure is PER DIRECTION and not a bidirectional aggregate. This resolves the three-times-repeated halving error on pcie-gen4, pcie-gen5 and the whole cxl-* family in this repo. Read this before comparing any PCIe or CXL number to an NVIDIA or AMD fabric number.
